newsitem.title: UK: BA expects to sell USAir stake at a profit.
newsitem.headline: BA expects to sell USAir stake at a profit.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Wednesday it expected to sell its 24.6 percent stake in USAir Group at a profit.
"We intend to sell at a premium to our original investment," a company spokesman said.

BA paid $400 million for its stake which is held in the form of preferred convertible bonds paying an annual interest rate of 7.0 percent. The spokesman said full conversion would equate to 19.29 million ordinary shares which would be worth $425 million at the opening price of USAir's ordinary shares on Wednesday.
USAir's ordinary share price opened at $22-1/8, compared to $15 when BA bought its first tranche of stock in 1993, rising to $21-1/2 when it bought the second tranche in May 1993.
BA would expect to attract a premium over the ordinary share price for the 7.0 percent preferred interest rate attached to its bonds, investment analysts said.
"But whether they can actually put 24.6 percent of the company into the market and achieve that is another matter," said a London-based investment analyst who declined to be named.

The analyst said that, if completed successfully, the sale should lead to an exceptional profit in BA's results of at least $200 million to restore a write-down it was compelled to make last year under U.S. accounting rules on half the value of the original stake.
